Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

"Qul" (Say): i.e., O Messenger of Allah.

"Ya ayyuha al-kafirun" (O disbelievers): i.e., the polytheists, namely al-Walid, al-'As, Ibn Khalaf and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib.

"La a'budu ma ta'budun" (I do not worship what you worship): i.e., of false deities, now.

"Wa la antum 'abidun ma a'bud" (Nor are you worshippers of what I worship): i.e., now.

"Wa la ana 'abidun ma 'abadtum" (Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped): i.e., in the future, forever.

"Wa la antum 'abidun ma a'bud" (Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship): i.e., in the future, forever, due to Allah's knowledge of that.

"Lakum dinukum" (For you is your religion): i.e., what you are upon of idolatry; you will never abandon it until you perish.

"Wa liya din" (And for me is my religion): i.e., Islam, which I will never abandon.

The meaning of the verses:

The Almighty's saying, ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ — these six noble verses were revealed in response to a proposal put forward by some polytheists, namely al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and Umayya ibn Khalaf, the gist of which was that the Prophet ﷺ should worship their gods for one year while they worship his God for one year, as a reconciliation between them and him and an ending of disputes in their view. The Messenger ﷺ did not answer them with anything until this surah was revealed: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾, i.e., say, O our Messenger, to these proposers of falsehood: O disbelievers in the divine revelation and in monotheism, polytheists who worship idols and images besides Allah the Exalted, ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ now, as you have proposed, ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ now, ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾ in the future, ever, ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ in the future, ever, because my Lord has decreed against you death upon disbelief and polytheism until you enter the Fire, because of what He knows of your hearts, your states, the ugliness of your conduct and the corruption of your deeds. ﴿For you is your religion﴾: I will not follow you in it. ﴿And for me is my religion﴾: you will not follow me in it. By this, Allah despaired His Messenger of the faith of this group, for whose faith the Prophet ﷺ had been hoping, and He despaired the polytheists of hoping that the Messenger ﷺ would agree to their corrupt proposal. These polytheists died in disbelief and none of them believed; some of them perished at Badr and others perished in Makkah upon disbelief and polytheism, and Allah the Mighty spoke the truth in what He reported about them: that they do not worship Allah in a way that saves them from His punishment and brings them into His mercy.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation of the creed of divine decree and destiny, and that the disbeliever is one who disbelieved from eternity and the believer is one who believed from eternity.

2- Allah's guardianship of His Messenger, protecting him from accepting the polytheists' false proposal.

3- Affirmation of the existence of a clear separation between the people of faith and the people of disbelief and polytheism.
